name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
prevalence_note: RSVGPF (Royal St. Vincent and the Grenadines Police Force) & ECCB 2025-2026: WhatsApp phishing and hijacked-contact money requests, impersonation of reputable vehicle dealers for import deposits, and ECCU bank/lottery scams dominate.
cross_border_note: Uses +1-784 within NANP and the ECCU; WhatsApp phishing links and spoofed +1 numbers frequently target Vincentians and diaspora contacts.

scams.name: RSVGPF-Warned WhatsApp Phishing & Account Hijack Scam
scams.name_en: Social-media/WhatsApp phishing link stealing 6-digit codes and soliciting emergency transfers
scams.signals_en: Scammer sends a phishing link or poses as a friend on WhatsApp asking for a 6-digit registration code, then hijacks the account to message contacts for urgent money transfers.
scams.legit_en: RSVGPF warns the public never to click suspicious social-media links or share verification codes.
bait_tactics: Say you never received any code and call the friend's regular voice line to verify who is texting.
Ask a local Kingstown or family question that an overseas hijacker could not answer.
Pretend the link fails to open on your old handset.

scams.name: RSVGPF-Warned Impersonation of Reputable Vehicle Dealers
scams.name_en: Fraudsters posing as established auto dealers on WhatsApp/phone to collect bogus vehicle deposits
scams.signals_en: Caller or social-media page impersonates a well-known SVG vehicle dealership offering discounted imports and pressing buyers to wire an upfront deposit to an unverified account.
scams.legit_en: Real Vincentian auto dealerships accept payments at their verified business premises under their registered corporate account.
bait_tactics: Tell them you are driving to the dealership's Kingstown lot right now to inspect the stock and pay at the cashier.
Ask why the beneficiary bank account name does not match the registered dealership name.
Request to inspect the customs paperwork at the showroom first.

scams.name: ECCB-Warned Fake Lottery Fee & Bank Card Phishing Call
scams.name_en: Unsolicited prize-claim fee demand or fake bank fraud call seeking card/OTP credentials
scams.signals_en: Caller claims the recipient won an overseas lottery requiring a release payment, or poses as an ECCU bank asking for card/OTP details to stop a bogus transaction.
scams.legit_en: ECCB advises never paying upfront fees for prizes and verifying suspicious bank calls directly with your local branch.
bait_tactics: Ask them to subtract the fee from the prize cheque before mailing it.
Say you will visit your bank branch in person rather than reading card details on the phone.
Pretend the phone line is crackling and ask them to repeat the company details slowly.
